top10: Value begins at deployment — Phase VI is continuous, never "done."
Data drift = inputs shift; Concept drift = meaning shifts.
Monitor performance + drift + business KPI + ops + fairness.
Retrain on schedule or on drift triggers — models decay.
Roll out safely: shadow → canary → full , rollback ready.
MLOps = DevOps + data & model versioning + drift management.
Model registry + audit trails + explainability = governance.
Learnings loop to Phase I — Iterate Often .
revision: Phase VI = deploy + monitor + maintain — value starts (not ends) at go-live.
Rollout ladder: shadow → canary → A/B → full , with rollback ready.
Data drift = input distribution changes; concept drift = X→Y meaning changes.
Monitor: performance, drift, business KPI, operational, fairness — with alert thresholds.
Retraining: scheduled / trigger-based / continuous → mini-cycle through Phases III–V.
MLOps: versioning (code+data+model), CI/CD, model registry , feature store , automation.
Governance: audit trails, explainability, human-in-the-loop, security .
Drive user adoption — unused models earn zero ROI.
Plan operations budget and eventual model retirement .
Learnings feed the next iteration → back to Phase I .
knowledgeCheck: Why is "deploy and forget" fatal for AI systems but merely risky for ordinary software?
Give a banking example of data drift and one of concept drift.
Match use cases to batch, real-time, and edge serving.
Describe the shadow → canary → full rollout ladder and its purpose.
What belongs in a production monitoring plan for a loan model?
Why must data and model versions be tracked alongside code?
What processes support user adoption of an AI system?
When should a model be retired?
How does Phase VI complete the CPMAI iteration loop?

examTips.heading: Memory Tricks
bullets: "Deployment is a birthday, not a funeral" — the model's life starts at go-live.
Drift memory: Data drift = inputs; Concept drift = meaning (X→Y) .
Speed test: milliseconds → real-time; nightly → batch; offline device → edge .

examTips.heading: Traps
bullets: Any " deploy and the project is complete " option → wrong.
"Roll out to 100% immediately" in high-stakes cases → prefer staged rollout.
